title: 102. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Solving Direct Proportion Problems
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value in a direct proportion using the constant of proportionality.
questions.question: If \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\), and \(y=12\) when \(x=3\), what is \(y\) when \(x=5\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\), write \(y=kx\). Using \(y=12\) and \(x=3\), we get \(12=3k\), so \(k=4\). Then for \(x=5\), \(y=4\times 5=20\). The alternative \(14\) adds the change in \(x\) to the old \(y\): \(12+(5-3)=14\).
questions.hint: Identify the quantity that stays constant per unit.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the equation that represents a direct proportion relationship.
questions.question: Which equation represents a direct proportion between \(y\) and \(x\)?
questions.explanation: A direct proportion has the form \(y=kx\), where \(k\) is a constant and the graph passes through the origin. The equation \(y=5x\) has this form with \(k=5\). The equation \(y=5x+2\) has an added constant, so it is not a direct proportion.
questions.hint: Compare a constant ratio with a constant difference.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of proportionality from a pair of directly proportional values.
questions.question: In a direct proportion, \(y=18\) when \(x=6\). What is the constant of proportionality \(k\)?
questions.explanation: For a direct proportion, \(y=kx\). Substitute \(y=18\) and \(x=6\): \(18=6k\). Dividing both sides by \(6\) gives \(k=3\). The alternative \(12\) subtracts the given values instead of finding their ratio: \(18-6=12\).
questions.hint: Write \(y=kx\) for the known pair and isolate \(k\).

questions.concept: Direct Proportion in Distance and Time
questions.learningObjective: Solve a distance problem using direct proportion at constant speed.
questions.question: A car travels \(180\text{ km}\) in \(3\text{ h}\) at a constant speed. How far will it travel in \(5\text{ h}\) at the same speed?
questions.explanation: At constant speed, distance is directly proportional to time. The speed is \(180\div 3=60\text{ km/h}\). In \(5\text{ h}\), the car travels \(60\times 5=300\text{ km}\). The alternative \(360\) doubles the old distance, although the time changes by a factor of \(\frac{5}{3}\), not \(2\).
questions.hint: Identify the quantity that stays constant per unit.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a cost problem using direct proportion.
questions.question: If \(4\) identical books cost \(36.00\text{ yuan}\), how much do \(7\) books cost at the same rate? Round to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The cost per book is \(\frac{36}{4}=9\text{ yuan}\), so the cost is \(7\times 9=63.00\text{ yuan}\). The alternative \(20.57\text{ yuan}\) comes from reversing the scale factor: \(36\times\frac{4}{7}\approx 20.57\).
questions.hint: Compare a constant ratio with a constant difference.

questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing table value using a constant ratio.
questions.question:
The table shows a direct proportion between \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
x & 2 & 4 & 6\\
\hline
y & 7 & 14 & ?
\end{array}
\]
What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: In a direct proportion, the ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\) is constant. Here, \(\frac{7}{2}=3.5\) and \(\frac{14}{4}=3.5\). For \(x=6\), \(y=3.5\times 6=21\). The alternative \(28\) doubles the latest \(y\)-value, although \(x\) changes from \(4\) to \(6\), not from \(4\) to \(8\).
questions.hint: Start from the known pair and decide which direction to scale.

questions.learningObjective: Use one known value pair to find another value in a direct proportion.
questions.question: If \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\), and \(y=45\) when \(x=9\), what is \(y\) when \(x=12\)?
questions.explanation: The constant is \(k=\frac{45}{9}=5\), so \(y=5\times 12=60\). The alternative \(48\) adds the increase in \(x\) directly to \(y\): \(45+(12-9)=48\); a direct proportion requires scaling.
questions.hint: Identify the quantity that stays constant per unit.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a scale drawing problem using direct proportion.
questions.question: On a map, \(3\text{ cm}\) represents \(18\text{ km}\). How many kilometres does \(5\text{ cm}\) represent?
questions.explanation: The map distance and actual distance are directly proportional. Since \(3\text{ cm}\) represents \(18\text{ km}\), \(1\text{ cm}\) represents \(18\div 3=6\text{ km}\). Therefore, \(5\text{ cm}\) represents \(6\times 5=30\text{ km}\). The alternative \(36\) doubles the known actual distance, although the map length changes by a factor of \(\frac{5}{3}\), not \(2\).
questions.hint: Compare a constant ratio with a constant difference.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a production problem using direct proportion.
questions.question: If \(5\) identical machines produce \(200\) parts in one hour, how many parts will \(8\) such machines produce in one hour at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The number of parts produced is directly proportional to the number of machines. One machine produces \(200\div 5=40\) parts per hour. Then \(8\) machines produce \(40\times 8=320\) parts per hour. The alternative \(203\) adds the three extra machines directly to the part count: \(200+(8-5)=203\).
questions.hint: Start from the known pair and decide which direction to scale.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a recipe scaling problem using direct proportion.
questions.question: A recipe for \(6\) people uses \(450\text{ g}\) of rice. How much rice is needed for \(10\) people at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The amount of rice is directly proportional to the number of people. For one person, the amount is \(450\div 6=75\text{ g}\). For \(10\) people, the amount is \(75\times 10=750\text{ g}\). The alternative \(270\text{ g}\) reverses the scaling factor, using \(450\times\frac{6}{10}=270\).
questions.hint: Identify the quantity that stays constant per unit.
